articles.title: Are people really refusing ‘Choosin’ Texas’? Or is monoculture just dead?
articles.summary: Don’t get mad if the hit country anthem isn’t for everyone. Nothing’s for everyone anymore.
articles.body:
Ella Langley's country anthem " Choosin' Texas " has spent nearly half the year atop the Billboard Hot 100. Its 24-week run has surpassed even Mariah Carey's "All I Want For Christmas Is You," making it the longest-running No. 1 single in US history.

And lots and lots of people say they've never heard it. Are they merely snobs who want to show off their proud ignorance of country music, as a recent argument-provoking Rolling Stone article suggested? Or is it that a No.1 hit song no longer reliably reaches the ears of a broad portion of the public?

The argument over "Choosin' Texas" and its apparent everywhere-and-nowhere quality, is about something larger than a single song, or even a genre. It's the newest case of the ongoing, much-discussed death of the "monoculture."

The monoculture is, or was, a collective frame of reference, a set of mass-cultural touchstones that everyone could assume everyone else knew about.

There was some indeterminate time in the past, the story goes, when a single piece of media could command the attention of everyone in the country: When everyone heard the same songs on the radio and MTV, watched the same few television networks and saw the same handful of movies playing in theaters, whether they liked them or not.

"When I was a brand manager, a hit that big was impossible to avoid because radio and TV put it in front of everyone whether you liked it or not," said Maria Rodas, an associate professor of marketing at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. "Now you can be one of the millions who had it on repeat all summer, or your feed just never showed it to you."

Cultural critics have been eulogizing this idea of monoculture since the dawn of the streaming era. What exactly constituted monoculture and when exactly it died, though, is less clear.

In a 2006 interview, rock critic Robert Christgau lamented the bygone era when "everybody listened to the same music on the radio." In 2011, the music journalist Touré mourned what he called "Massive Music Moments," something he declared that no one under 25 had experienced. The popularity and success of Lady Gaga, Adele and Kanye West, he wrote at the time, could not compare to the ubiquity once enjoyed by Michael Jackson's "Thriller" or Nirvana's "Nevermind."

If the cultural landscape seemed fragmented then, it would only become more so. With the benefit of hindsight, music journalists are now waxing nostalgic about more recent eras. Earlier this year, The Hollywood Reporter declared 2014 as " The Last Time Everyone Watched the Same Thing ." Another article this year from Rolling Stone proclaimed that monoculture ended in 2016.

"That was the last time it felt as though there was a coherent popular culture," the magazine's music editor, Jeff Ihaza, wrote, "before everything fractured into algorithmic bits spread across hours of screen time."

The word "monoculture" comes from agriculture, referring to the practice of cultivating a single crop on a plot of land. In pre-industrial times, farmers planted an array of different crops in the same space, creating a diverse environment that mimicked natural ecosystems. When the Europeans colonized the Americas, they began planting single commercial crops such as sugar or tobacco over large areas, to sell overseas.

Though the technique was more economically efficient, it introduced new problems: A pest that infected one plant was likely to infect them all, threatening to wipe out entire harvests. Planting a single crop also led to faster depletion of nutrients in soil.

Plant monoculture also had aesthetic purposes. For generations, American streets and parks showcased the tall, stately pillars of rows and rows of elm trees. The arrival of Dutch elm disease not only ravaged these green spaces, but discredited the whole goal of aiming for such uniformity.

Like its agricultural and horticultural counterparts, the monoculture of era-defining music, TV and movies seemed alluring on the surface. Having common cultural references could bring people together, making society feel more cohesive and connected.

But on closer examination, the perils became clear. Pop culture in the pre-social internet, pre-streaming era was largely dictated top-down by industry gatekeepers, designed to appeal to as many people as possible. It might have been easier in those days to make small talk with coworkers, but it was harder to discover work without the backing of the industry machine.

"As comforting as it was in olden times to know that just about anyone you'd meet on the street would've heard the latest Madonna single or would know what happened on Dallas that week, if you were the sort of person who preferred The Young Ones and Hüsker Dü, you could feel pretty excluded from the cultural conversation," Noel Murray wrote for the AV Club in 2009.

And even culture that seemed ubiquitous could be inconsequential or ignored in some circles. People longing for the days of monoculture often point to sitcoms such as "Seinfeld" and "Friends," which drew millions of viewers. But those shows were less universal than people now make them seem.

"Everybody did not watch 'Seinfeld.' Everybody did not watch 'Friends,'" NPR pop culture correspondent Linda Holmes wrote in 2024. "In fact, some 'everybodies' pointed out that it owed an awful lot to 'Living Single.'"

Today, popular culture is produced from the bottom up, propelled by social media recommendation algorithms, said Kyle Chayka, a staff writer for The New Yorker and author of "Filterworld: How Algorithms Flattened Culture." Theoretically, this means that smaller, independent artists can release their work on social media platforms and directly reach the audiences most inclined to appreciate it. It also means that users can more easily access media that better aligns with their tastes.

But this creates a fragmented landscape where people are consuming media in line with their own interests, while fewer and fewer people seem to be consuming the same things as one another.

Meanwhile, algorithms are vulnerable to manipulation. Certain features can help songs or videos achieve maximum success on social media platforms, giving creators and artists incentive to engineer those features into their work.

Paradoxically, then, this system of individual artists pursuing individual success creates a new kind of sameness, which Chayka and others also describe as monoculture. The same phenomenon applies to minimalist interiors in independent coffee shops, all-neutral home decorating schemes and the uniformity of facial features and bodies on screen. The old monoculture might be dead, if it ever existed, but a new one has taken its place.

"We're not all watching the same exact TV show, but there are a hundred versions of 'Love Is Blind' and 'Love Island' or 'Real Housewives,' and we're all watching slightly different versions of the same genre of thing," Chayka said.

Rodas added, "Culture has splintered into a thousand niches, and inside each niche the safe, familiar thing wins."

There are big events that still seem to command widespread attention — the World Cup, the New York Knicks' NBA championship run, Taylor Swift's wedding, the cyclosporiasis outbreak affecting iceberg lettuce — and this summer in particular inspired a flurry of commentary wondering whether the old monoculture had returned. But depending on one's interests and algorithm, it's still easier than ever to miss out on something popular.

What does it mean, then, that 2026's biggest hit didn't even register for a vast swath of listeners?

"You can pay close attention to music for every day of your life, and still miss the overwhelming majority of what's out there to be heard," rock critic Steven Hyden wrote in a recent Substack column. "Even really, really big songs like 'Choosin' Texas.'"

articles.title: Sydney Sweeney, al más puro estilo Pamela Anderson: luce el mítico bikini de ‘Los vigilantes de la playa’
articles.standfirst: Esta es la primera reacción desde la polémica generada por su anuncio
articles.summary: Esta es la primera reacción desde la polémica generada por su anuncio
articles.body: Sydney Sweeney ha hecho oídos sordos a su última polémica por el anuncio de la casa de apuestas Novig. Esta plataforma estadounidense utilizó a la actriz para promocionar sus contenidos, pero lo que fue objeto de crítica es que lo hiciera totalmente desnuda, tapándose con los diferentes materiales deportivos que iba mencionando. Eso provocó que las redes sociales y diferentes colectivos se pronunciaran en contra de la intérprete de ‘La Monja’. Incluso, se llegó a crear un trend en redes sociales. Sin embargo, Sydney Sweeney parece no estar demasiado al tanto del revuelo generado y, la primera aparición desde entonces ha sido luciendo el mítico bikini de Pamela Anderson en ‘Los vigilantes de la playa’. Estamos hablando de un bañador rojo de una única pieza, de corte bastante alto en la pierna. Gracias a este look en la serie, Pamela Anderson se convirtió en símbolo a nivel mundial y esta prenda en una moda de baño única en la época. Y lo cierto es que Sweeney no ha sido la única intérprete que se ha atrevido con él con el paso de los años. “Cuando tu hombre te lleva a la luna”, dice el título del post publicado por la actriz. Este posado no ha sido la única imagen publicada por Sweeney. Como amante del deporte, ha mostrado diferentes actividades que ha realizado con Scoot Braun, su pareja. Desde un paseo en yate, surf, fiestas y numerosas postales para guardar en su recuerdo. En los comentarios del post no parecen recordar lo ocurrido hace apenas un mes con el polémico anuncio. De hecho, sólo hay mensajes positivos para la actriz: “Este viaje será imposible de superar”, “Me alegro de que seas feliz”, “La vida más indiferente y pacífica. Sigue adelante hermosa”.

articles.title: Paula Santoro canta músicas do Clube da Esquina em álbum feito na Espanha com o pianista de jazz Germán Kucich | G1
articles.standfirst: Intitulado 'Alunar', o disco homenageia Milton Nascimento na música inédita 'Nave', parceria do violonista Leo Minax com o letrista Chico Amaral.
articles.summary: Intitulado 'Alunar', o disco homenageia Milton Nascimento na música inédita 'Nave', parceria do violonista  Leo Minax com o letrista Chico Amaral.
articles.body:
A cantora mineira Paula Santoro posa com o pianista argentino Germán Kucich no Camaleon Music Studio, em Madrid, onde gravou o álbum 'Alunar — Foto: Acervo pessoal Paula Santoro

♬ Após turnê pela Europa, Paula Santoro voltou ao Brasil na manhã desta sexta-feira, 2 de outubro, com álbum quase pronto na bagagem. A convite do pianista de jazz Germán Kucich, músico argentino residente em Madrid, Espanha, a cantora mineira gravou na última quinzena de setembro um álbum, “Alunar”, com músicas de compositores do Clube da Esquina.

Apresentada na voz de Milton Nascimento em álbum de 1970, a música-título “Alunar” é a primeira composição da parceria de Lô Borges (1952 – 2025) com o irmão Márcio Borges.

Milton Nascimento, aliás, é homenageado na única música inédita do álbum “Alunar”, cujo repertório é composto basicamente por standards do cancioneiro mineiro. A música inédita se chama “Nave” e é uma parceria do cantor, compositor e violonista mineiro Leo Minax – músico que reside em Madrid há cerca de 30 anos e que toca com Germán Kucich – com o letrista Chico Amaral. Foi através de Minax que Kucich chegou ao nome de Paula Santoro.

Paula Santoro e Kucich gravaram o álbum “Alunar” no Camaleon Music Studio, em Madrid, com os toques dos músicos Marc Pinyol (bateria) e Toño Miguel (contrabaixo). Um quarto músico, o percussionista Tiki Cantero, ainda vai se juntar à banda do disco, gravando as percussões em janeiro em Buenos Aires, na Argentina.

Com 12 músicas, o álbum “Alunar” reapresenta as músicas dos compositores mineiros com o toque do jazz já recorrente na sonoridade dos instrumentistas.

Além das já citadas “Alunar” e “Nave”, o repertório inclui “A página do relâmpago elétrico” (Beto Guedes e Ronaldo Bastos, 1977), “Cravo e canela” (Milton Nascimento e Ronaldo Bastos, 1971), “Fazenda” (Nelson Angelo, 1976), “Novena” (Milton Nascimento e Márcio Borges, 1978), “Paixão e fé” (Tavinho Moura e Fernando Brant, 1977), “Pão e água” (Lô Borges, Márcio Borges e Roger Mota, 1978), “Pensamento” (Milton Nascimento e Fernando Brant, 1986), “Saídas e bandeiras” (Milton Nascimento e Fernando Brant, 1972), “Um gosto de sol” (Milton Nascimento e Ronaldo Bastos, 1972) e “Viver de amor” (Toninho Horta e Ronaldo Bastos, 1976).

O álbum “Alunar” tem lançamento previsto para o primeiro semestre de 2027.

articles.title: Trio de jazz Caixa Cubo toca Caetano Veloso e Gilberto Gil em 'Ultracooked', álbum programado para novembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Grupo paulistano também regrava choro de Garoto e presta tributos a João Donato e a Hermeto Pascoal.
articles.summary: Grupo paulistano também regrava choro de Garoto e presta tributos a João Donato e a Hermeto Pascoal.
articles.body:
O trio paulistano de jazz Caixa Cubo lança em 20 de novembro o nono álbum do grupo, 'Ultracooked' — Foto: Rebecca Figueiredo / Divulgação

♬ Nono álbum do trio Caixa Cubo, grupo paulistano de jazz que já vem atuando além das fronteiras do Brasil, “Ultracooked” tem lançamento programado para 20 de novembro em LP, CD e edição digital.

Ao longo das 13 faixas do álbum “Ultracooked”, Henrique Gomide (piano, teclados e sintetizadores), João Fideles (bateria e percussão) e Noa Stroeter (baixo acústico e elétrico) abordam música de Caetano Veloso (“Odara”, de 1977), tocam dois temas do cancioneiro de Gilberto Gil – “Expresso 2222” (1972) e “Essa é pra tocar no rádio” (1975), ambas ouvidas no álbum “Ultracooked” com a voz do cantor Zé Leônidas, convidado do trio – e voltam ao repertório do compositor e violonista Garoto (1915 – 1955), a quem o Caixa Cubo já dedicou um songbook instrumental há oito anos, “Enigma – A música de Garoto”, álbum editado em 2018.

De Garoto, o trio reaviva “Jorge do Fusa”, choro composto em 1950 originalmente como tema instrumental, letrado na sequência pelo compositor Mário Albanese e gravado de forma caseira por Albanese e Garoto, ainda naquele ano de 1950, trinta anos antes do primeiro registro fonográfico oficial do choro, apresentado em disco em 1980.

Entre temas como “Cabaré” (faixa gravada com a guitarra de Edson Woiski), “Cara do meio”, “Coisa redonda”, “Marea”, “Ribe” e “Superkid”, o Caixa Cubo presta reverências a Hermeto Pascoal (1936 – 2025) e a João Donato (1934 – 2023). As faixas se chamam “Hermeto” e “Donato”, respectivamente, e ambas trazem as vozes faladas dos homenageados, embutidas na gravação.

Formatado com produção musical orquestrada pelo próprio Caixa Cubo em colaboração com Frederico Pacheco, o álbum “Ultracooked” foi gravado no O&O Studios, em São Paulo (SP), cidade natal do trio. Já a masterização foi feita por Casper Sutton no Gearbox Studios, em Londres, Inglaterra, sede da gravadora que edita o álbum, Far Out Recordings.

“Ultracooked” sucede o álbum “Modo avião” na discografia iniciada em 2012 pelo trio Caixa Cubo.

articles.title: Stray Kids se junta ao BTS e decide não participar do Grammy após polêmica com nova categoria | G1
articles.standfirst: Gravadora confirmou que artistas não disputarão edição de 2027 em meio a críticas sobre criação de categoria 'Melhor Performance de Música Pop Asiática'.
articles.summary: Gravadora confirmou que artistas não disputarão edição de 2027 em meio a críticas sobre criação de categoria 'Melhor Performance de Música Pop Asiática'.
articles.body:
Stray Kids no Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

O grupo de K-pop Stray Kids não inscreveu nenhum trabalho para concorrer ao Grammy 2027.

A informação foi dada pela gravadora do octeto, a JYP Entertainment, em comunicado enviado à imprensa.

Não houve uma explicação precisa sobre o motivo, mas a decisão do Stray Kids, que esteve no Brasil este ano para participar do Rock in Rio , acontece após a criação da categoria "Melhor Performance de Música Pop Asiática", o que gerou críticas por colocar o gênero fora das grandes categorias.

Em julho, o BTS também anunciou que não disputaria o Grammy e foi mais direto sobre a razão.

"Decidimos não inscrever nossa música no Grammy este ano. Esperamos que a música possa ser ouvida e receber amor por si só, sem ser dividida por região ou idioma. Agradecemos aos ARMYs e a todos que estão sempre conosco", diz o comunicado compartilhado nos perfis dos integrantes do grupo.

O Grammy anunciou, em 16 de junho, a criação de cinco novas categorias que valerão a partir da 69ª edição, agendada para 7 de fevereiro de 2027.

Entre as novidades apresentadas, a introdução da categoria "Melhor Música Latina" estabeleceu um critério técnico que deixa o mercado fonográfico brasileiro praticamente de fora da disputa principal.

Isso porque, de acordo com o novo regulamento, o prêmio é destinado exclusivamente a compositores de obras inéditas escritas predominantemente em espanhol, exigindo que, no mínimo, 51% da letra esteja nesse idioma.

"Melhor Performance de Música Pop Asiática" (voltada a gêneros como K-pop, J-pop e C-pop);

"Melhor Colaboração ou Performance em Dupla/Grupo de R&B";

"Melhor Performance Vocal Pop Tradicional";

"Melhor Álbum de Música Folclórica Tradicional".

articles.title: José Mariano Benítez de Lugo, primer abogado que enfrentó a los fondos buitre en España: "Es una lucha de David contra Goliat"
articles.standfirst: El letrado recalca que los decretos del Gobierno en materia de vivienda son “un rollo”
articles.summary: El letrado recalca que los decretos del Gobierno en materia de vivienda son “un rollo”
articles.body: ‘La Revuelta’, programa que presenta y dirige David Broncano en La 1 en ‘access prime time’, echó el cierre a una nueva semana. El invitado para la ocasión en el Teatro Albéniz de Madrid fue José Mariano Benítez de Lugo Guillén, abogado con 63 años de experiencia y que llevó a juicio a varios fondos buitre por la compra de vivienda pública. Broncano le presentó tirando de ironía: “Lleva siendo abogado desde los años 50 y es uno de los mejores abogados del país”. El letrado entró entre aplausos, con casco de mano en moto y un maletín de color negro, agradeciendo el recibimiento. Benítez de Lugo participó en algunos procesos judiciales y penales de renombre, como la acusación popular contra Rajoy en el caso Gürtel, los papeles de Bárcenas o el caso Madrid Arena. También fue el primer letrado en enfrentarse a la venta de viviendas públicas a fondos buitre en España. El asunto sigue de actualidad por lo que está sucediendo con Maricarmen. En referencia al expresidente del Gobierno, reveló que vivía en su misma urbanización y añadió: “Los escoltan siempre me saludaban cuando salía de mi casa a trabajar hacia el bufete de abogados, pero cuando me cruzaba con él ni me miraba”. Con lo que respecta a los fondos buitre dice que es como una lucha de “David contra Goliat”. Eso sí, el letrado no termina de entender algunos aspectos de la justicia española: “Hay un problema de equilibrio de poderes complicado porque los jueces tienen mucho poder y creo que muchos se inmiscuyen en campos ajenos, pero yo me opongo a todo lo que considero que es injusto”. Asimismo, quiso destacar a los culpables de lo que está sucediendo con los desahucios y el asunto de la vivienda: “Las entidades públicas de la época del PP que vendieron viviendas públicas, allá por 2014, los fondos buitres por comprar y los jueces, que son incapaces de contemplar que las leyes hay que interpretarlas conforme a la realidad social que se deben aplicar en el tiempo actual”. “Tengo una deuda con la sociedad y la intento cumplir. Tengo que hacer lo que debo hacer: defender a la gente vulnerable en todos los niveles de mi vida, pero me arrastro para poder llegar a un acuerdo con los fondos buitre, son voraces, les da todo igual, pero son todos paños calientes”, siguió profiriendo Benítez de Lugo. Posteriormente, charlaron de diversas anécdotas y casos relacionados con los fondos buitre que gestionó a lo largo de sus 63 años de experiencia. Broncano quiso preguntarle acerca de quién cree que gobernará tras las próximas elecciones generales, a lo que el invitado contestó: “Una cosa es lo que yo crea y otra lo que desee, pero tengo mis serias preocupaciones de que el PP gane”. Del mismo modo, sobre los dos decretos que el Gobierno prevé aprobar este viernes, 2 de octubre, en materia de vivienda añadió lo siguiente: “Hay algunas cosas positivas, pero no me gustan los decretos ómnibus. Son 94 páginas y es un rollo de coj****”. El presentador de ‘La Revuelta’ quiso saber cuál es la solución que propone al respecto: “El problema es que la vivienda es un bien de mercado que tienen los capitalistas salvajes. Frenar eso con una mayoría parlamentaria precaria es imposible”. Para finalizar, el letrado respondió a las preguntas clásicas para cerrar la semana en ‘La Revuelta’.

articles.title: Did you know Hayden Panettiere had wellness check week before she passed away? - Report
articles.summary: New reports reveal that Hayden Panettiere underwent a wellness check just days before her passing, raising questions about her final days. The investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death continues as fans mourn the loss of the beloved star.
articles.body: As the investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s passing continues, new details about the days leading up to her passing have been shared online. According to recent reports, the ‘Heroes’ actress had faced a wellness check only days before she was found in an unresponsive state.Hayden Panettiere had a wellness check before her passingAccording to reports shared by US Weekly, the L.A. County Sheriff’s Department had performed a wellness check on the star’s home in Los Angeles. They shared that the department had received a call from someone around 10 PM on August 9, who had requested that they perform a wellness check on the star.The call allegedly was made by someone who was “concerned” for the well-being of a white woman in West Hollywood and about not answering the phone. The reports did not reveal who the caller was.About Hayden PanettiereHayden Panettiere, best known for her work in 'Nashville,' ‘Scream 2,' ‘Malcolm in the Middle,' and ‘Ice Princess,' passed away on August 16, only a few days before her 37th birthday. She was found by her on-and-off boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother, Zach, who saw that she was unresponsive in an apartment in the city of Greenville and soon after called the police.The police department there issued a statement that during the preliminary investigation, her passing did “not indicate any signs of foul play or suspicious circumstances.” Other than that, there were “no signs of trauma (that) would have contributed to the death.” The official cause of her passing was reported last month: “toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol, and quetiapine."Hayden’s publicist confirmed that, along with all of the things that are going on around Hayden’s passing, they are continuing the investigation into what happened in that room. Her statement, which was given to CNN, read, “The investigation remains ongoing, and the circumstances surrounding the case are complex. We must all continue to remain patient and allow the investigative process to unfold.”Panettiere is survived by her 11-year-old daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with ex-fiancé Wladimir Klitschko. articles.title: Why replacing Vikrant Massey with Jitendra Kumar worked for ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’, EXPLAINS the director
articles.summary: ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’ continues its strong box office run, with worldwide collections reaching Rs 333.29 crore by Day 27.
articles.body: ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’ continues its strong box office run, with worldwide collections reaching Rs 333.29 crore by Day 27. As the film keeps drawing audiences, director Gurmmeet Singh has shared insights into how it was made, from key creative choices to the actors' input in shaping their roles and the origins of its standout moments. He spoke about casting Jitendra Kumar as Bablu Pandit in place of Vikrant Massey, and about Mohitt Maalik's take on Birju Lohar, reflecting on how the characters have changed over the years.Gurmmeet Singh on recasting in 'Mirzapur: The Movie'Speaking to SCREEN about the recasting and how it shaped the narrative, Gurmmeet said, “I think the beauty about a make-believe world or doing something creative and fiction is that as an artiste, one always needs to have choices, right? As creators, as actors, what’s the one thing that we all desperately want? It’s to have choices and to be able to make that choice. And it’s a good lesson to learn that everyone needs to be able to follow what their heart is telling them to do. No story, no character, no journey is bound down by anybody, right? The show will always move forward, and that’s the beauty we can take forward from this, that with Jitendra coming in, it brought a new energy into the show. It also gave the film its own identity.”How 'Mirzapur: The Movie' reimagined BabluThe director went on to explain that the change in casting gave the team a chance to rethink Bablu and place him closer to the centre of the story. He said, “It gave it its own life, which is very different from the show, which is what we always wanted anyways. So it became a blessing in disguise. We were able to reimagine Bablu and give him more agency. The Bablu in the show was almost aiding his brother and was a victim, never having agency or an agenda of his own. But this Bablu is playing the game. He’s the one driving the narrative. So, I think that’s a great learning we’ve taken away, to always use your setbacks to your advantage, because that’s what creativity is meant to do. Look ahead, and with the film doing as well as it has, I think it only opens up so many doors for us.”'Mirzapur: The Movie' release date and cast‘Mirzapur: The Movie’ hit theatres on September 4, with a cast that includes Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal, Jitendra Kumar, Rasika Dugal, Shweta Tripathi, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Abhishek Banerjee and Mohitt Maalik.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Chris Hemsworth’s daughter India Rose wins the Bull-Riding competition; elated father celebrates the victory with a sweet post
articles.summary: Chris Hemsworth celebrates his daughter India Rose's victory as the only girl in a bull-riding competition, showcasing her adventurous spirit and family pride.
articles.body: Chris Hemsworth is celebrating a big win for his 14-year-old daughter, India Rose, after she took first place in a bull-riding competition where she was the only girl competing. The actor shared videos from the event on Instagram, showing his daughter riding a bucking bull before celebrating the result with her.Hemsworth called his daughter “savage” in his post and proudly pointed out that she was the only girl in the competition, yet she won. The moment also gave fans a glimpse into the adventurous side of the teenager, who has previously been involved in equestrian sports and motocross.India Rose takes on an all-boys bull-riding competitionIn one of the videos Hemsworth shared, India Rose can be seen holding on as the bull moves around the arena. Another clip captures a father-daughter moment before the competition, with Hemsworth cheering her on and calling her a champion bull rider.The actor jokingly asked his daughter whether she would be able to stay on for seven seconds. India immediately corrected him, explaining that the target was eight seconds. Hemsworth then laughed off the correction, responding, “Eight seconds, what do I know?”The videos quickly drew attention because India was not simply participating alongside other young riders; she was the only female contestant in the competition. Hemsworth's proud reaction made the achievement even more personal for his followers.Why did Chris Hemsworth name his daughter India Rose?India's name has its own connection to the country, something Hemsworth explained years before her latest sporting achievement.During a 2019 conversation with news agency IANS while promoting 'Men in Black: International', Hemsworth was asked about his daughter's name. He explained that his wife, Elsa Pataky, had spent a considerable amount of time in India and said that was where the name originally came from.The actor also spoke warmly about his own experience in the country. Hemsworth had travelled to India in 2018 to film his Netflix project 'Extraction', then known as 'Dhaka', shooting scenes in Ahmedabad and Mumbai.He described the experience as both intimidating and exciting, particularly because of the crowds that gathered during filming. He also spoke about the warmth he and the production received while working in the country.The name had another story behind itHemsworth had actually spoken about the name several years earlier, shortly after India Rose was born.In a 2012 interview with E! News, he explained that he had always liked names such as Indie or Indiana, while Pataky liked India. Rather than settling on one immediately, the couple decided the name would work whether their child was a boy or a girl. Hemsworth said it eventually “just seemed to fit.”The later IANS interview added another layer to that story by explaining the family's personal connection with India.When India Rose appeared alongside her father Chris Hemsworth?Bull riding is not the only unusual experience India has shared with her famous parents. She also appeared alongside Hemsworth in the Marvel film 'Thor: Love and Thunder', playing Love, the daughter of Gorr the God Butcher. Her father has previously described the children's involvement in the film as a one-off family experience rather than the beginning of a professional acting career.India has also been seen taking part in equestrian activities and motocross. Her mother, Spanish actress Elsa Pataky, has shared glimpses of their family's interest in horses and outdoor activities.Chris Hemsworth’s family life away from HollywoodHemsworth and Pataky married in 2010 and have three children: India Rose and twin sons Sasha and Tristan.The family has largely based its life in Australia, with Hemsworth and Pataky often sharing outdoor moments rather than keeping their children closely tied to Hollywood. articles.body: Supermodel Linda Evangelista owned this New York City penthouse for over 25 years; however, according to recent reports, it has been confirmed that the star finally sold off the property. The West Chelsea loft has seen her through her entire career, during which she established herself as one of the biggest names in the industry. Here is a look inside her stunning property that she had owned since 2001.Inside Linda Evangelista’s NYC penthouseThe supermodel purchased the home all the way back in 2001. She invested around USD 1.4 million for the property, and it was her main home for almost 25 years. Her penthouse is located inside the Spears Building, which is a former 19th-century manufacturing plant that was later turned into a 6-story loft condominium.The New York Post reported that the stunning property offers a view of the Manhattan skyline and features modern architecture and interior design. Spanning 4,022 square feet, the property features a total of 4 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms. Some of the other defining features of the property include the 13-foot ceilings, skylights, exposed brick walls that have been painted white, along with dark polished concrete floors, and a wood-burning fireplace in the primary living space.The report further revealed that the penthouse also has high-end appliances all over the house, along with a compact built-in bar, a hidden home office nook, and a galley chef's kitchen fitted with white cabinetry and butcher-block counters. The entire home is built on an open space, with the living area offering a premium view of the surrounding areas.More about the supermodel suiteThe main bedroom suite located in the penthouse features an en-suite spa bathroom that also has a soaking tub, along with a massive walk-in dressing room lined with six floor-to-ceiling custom closets tailored to her wardrobe. However, one of the best qualities of the apartment comes from the large windows that offer a direct view to the residents of the room of the High Line.Linda Evangelista’s home’s crown jewel; the private balconyOne of the best features of Evangelista’s penthouse is the 2,500-square-foot private rooftop terrace. This outdoor space includes wood decking with a dedicated lounge and sunbathing zone, a shaded dining area underneath a wooden pergola, as well as a built-in outdoor grilling and entertaining station for guests to enjoy.Keanu Reeves once stayed on the propertyThe property first went up on the market in 2024, when the asking price was listed as USD 9.45 million. However, since not many offers were made to purchase the property, she briefly rented out the property to Hollywood star Keanu Reeves, who is best known for his work in the ‘Matrix’ franchise, along with the ‘John Wick’ franchise, 'Speed,' ‘Point Break,' 'Constantine,' and many others. He had been in New York working on the Broadway production of ‘Waiting for Godot.' Reports revealed that the actor used to pay USD 45,000 to stay at Linda’s property.Linda Evangelista officially sells her property for USD 6.75 millionLinda Evangelista recently sold her property for USD 6.75 million. Compared to the original asking price, CityRealty reported that the supermodel had to price down the home for the official sale quite a bit. However, she still turned over a brief profit on the property since she originally bought it for around USD 1.4 million. articles.title: Quote of the day by Justin Bieber: ‘The blessing is not about being able to receive as much as it is being in a position to give back to others,’ a lesson in gratitude and purpose from the American singer
articles.summary: Explore Justin Bieber's powerful quote on gratitude and the meaning of success. Discover how giving back transforms one’s achievements into opportunities for others.
articles.body: Success can change a person's life, but Justin Bieber once suggested that the real value of success may not lie in what someone receives. It may lie in what they are able to do for others once they have been given an opportunity. For an artist who had already experienced extraordinary success as a teenager, the thought offered a different way of looking at everything he had gained so quickly.Today’s quote of the day by Justin Bieber reads: “The blessing is not about being able to receive as much as it is being in a position to give back to others.”What does Justin Bieber’s quote mean?Bieber's quote is really about what happens after a person receives something they have worked for. The words were shared by Bieber on social media in December 2011. An archived record of his posts on the Justin Bieber Wiki preserves the message from December 7, 2011, along with the hashtag "#blessed." Success is often viewed through the things people can point to: a bigger home, a successful career, awards, money or recognition. But Bieber's words shift attention away from possession. Being "in a position to give back" means that having more can also create an opportunity to help someone else.That does not necessarily mean giving away money. Giving back can take many forms. Someone might share their knowledge, support another person's dream, offer their time or simply use an opportunity to open a door for somebody else. There is also something personal about the way Bieber described a blessing. Instead of treating success as something that belongs entirely to the person who receives it, he connected it with responsibility.For someone who became famous as a teenager, the idea carried particular weight. His career had given him opportunities that most people his age could only imagine. The quote suggests that those opportunities become more meaningful when they can benefit other people too.Why is Justin Bieber’s quote still relevant today?The quote hits differently today because so much of what we call success is put on display. A quick scroll through social media can turn followers, views, new purchases and career wins into numbers that people use to measure how well they are doing. People can become so focused on getting ahead that they forget to ask what their progress can mean beyond themselves. Bieber's quote offers a simpler way of looking at it. Receiving something good is only one part of the story. What someone chooses to do with that opportunity can matter just as much.That idea applies far beyond celebrities. A student who gets a scholarship can help another student understand the application process. Someone who finds success in a career can mentor a newcomer. A person who has learned from difficult experiences can share those lessons with someone facing a similar situation. The scale may be different, but the principle remains the same: having an advantage can also create a chance to help someone else.Justin Bieber’s early lifeJustin Drew Bieber was born on March 1, 1994, in London, Ontario, Canada, and grew up in Stratford. Music became part of his life early, and he taught himself to play instruments including the drums, guitar, piano and trumpet.His mother, Pattie Mallette, began uploading videos of him performing on YouTube. What started as a way for relatives and friends to see him sing gradually turned into something much bigger.Bieber also took part in a local singing competition when he was 12 and finished second. The videos started reaching more people and that growing online buzz eventually caught the eye of talent manager Scooter Braun. Bieber later met Usher, setting him on a path toward a professional music career. His 2010 memoir, 'First Step 2 Forever: My Story', described that journey from performing in Stratford to entering the music industry.Justin Bieber’s rise to fameBieber's career took off quickly. After releasing his debut EP, 'My World', in 2009, he followed it with 'My World 2.0' a year later. The album topped the Billboard 200, and the teenager who had first found an audience through online videos was suddenly performing for fans around the world. By then, Bieber had built a huge following online. Millions were keeping up with him on social media, while his YouTube videos were drawing more than a billion views. So when he wrote about giving back in 2011, he was already far beyond the teenager people had first noticed in those early videos. He had already experienced what it felt like to have millions of people listening to him, watching him and following his career.That journey gives the quote another layer. His success was something he had received through talent, opportunity and the support of people around him. His words suggest that the next step was not simply to keep collecting more, but to find ways to pass something on.For Bieber, the idea of being blessed was therefore closely tied to what he could give. And that is what makes the quote continue to resonate: success may feel rewarding when it arrives, but it can mean even more when it becomes useful to someone else.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: ‘Gondhal’ exclusive previews from October 9; Santosh Davakhar’s film to release in six languages after Oscar entry
articles.summary: Santosh Davakhar’s Marathi psychological thriller ‘Gondhal’, which has been selected as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, is set to have
articles.body: Santosh Davakhar’s Marathi psychological thriller ‘Gondhal’, which has been selected as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards, is set to have exclusive preview screenings from October 9. The film will screen in Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad and Bengaluru ahead of its wider worldwide theatrical release.The previews will begin on October 9 across four theatres each in Mumbai and Pune, followed by screenings in Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai and Hyderabad. The special screenings will be presented in Marathi and Hindi, giving audiences an opportunity to watch the film ahead of its multilingual theatrical release.Written and directed by Davakhar, ‘Gondhal’ is set against the backdrop of Maharashtra’s traditional Gondhal folk performance, a ritual that combines devotional storytelling, music, percussion and dance. The film explores this cultural form through the lens of a psychological thriller, bringing together themes of tradition, desire, human emotions and hidden tensions.The film stars Ishita Deshmukh, Kishor Kadam and Yogesh Sohoni in key roles. It combines elements rooted in rural Maharashtra with themes that extend beyond its regional setting.‘Gondhal’ has also travelled through the festival circuit. Davakhar received the Silver Peacock for Best Director at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI), while the film won the FIPRESCI Award at the Bengaluru International Film Festival. The cast and makers were also recently honoured by Maharashtra Chief Minister Shri Devendra Fadnavis. The film’s selection as India’s official entry for the 99th Academy Awards has further brought it into the spotlight.Speaking about the exclusive previews, Santosh Davakhar said, “For us, these previews are more than just early screenings; they are an opportunity to bring Gondhal back to audiences for whom the theatrical experience was always at the heart of the film. This is a story born from Maharashtra’s cultural soil, and we have always believed that its atmosphere, sound and visual world should be experienced collectively in a theatre. After the honour of representing India at the Oscars, it feels especially meaningful to open the doors of the film to audiences and let them experience Gondhal for themselves. I hope viewers enter the theatre without preconceived notions and allow the story, the culture and its psychological journey to speak for themselves.”After the preview screenings, ‘Gondhal’ will release worldwide in Marathi, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Kannada.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Dino Morea summoned again by EOW in Mithi River desilting case, questioned over alleged links
articles.summary: Actor Dino Morea has once again come under the scanner of the Mumbai Police’s Economic Offences Wing (EOW) in connection with the alleged Mithi River
articles.body: Actor Dino Morea has once again come under the scanner of the Mumbai Police’s Economic Offences Wing (EOW) in connection with the alleged Mithi River desilting scam. The actor was questioned by the agency after investigators reportedly found phone records indicating his contact with people linked to the case. Morea and his brother Santino Rocco Morea had also been questioned by the EOW in May 2025.According to a report published by Hindustan Times, an EOW officer said, “We summoned [Dino] Morea after investigators came across phone records indicating contact with some people linked to the case.”The investigation is also looking into the business links between the Morea family and those accused in the case. According to the report, Santino Rocco Morea and Punita Kadam, wife of arrested accused Ketan Kadam, were directors in UBO Ridez Private Limited. Investigators are examining financial transactions involving the Kadams and Santino, besides looking into how Ketan Kadam’s desilting company, Woder India LLP, secured civic contracts.Ketan Kadam was arrested on May 7 and is among the accused booked in the case. The EOW has alleged that the irregularities in the Mithi River desilting project caused the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) a loss of Rs 65.54 crore. The case involves allegations of financial irregularities, inflated tenders and corrupt practices.The agency has also arrested Jayesh Joshi, who is associated with Virgo Specialties Private Limited, a Mumbai-based industrial product manufacturer. Investigators are looking into the alleged role of middlemen and companies involved in supplying or renting specialised equipment for the desilting work.The EOW’s probe has also focused on the tendering process. According to investigators, some BMC officials travelled to Kochi in October 2020 to purchase desilting equipment from Matprop Technical Services Private Limited. Subsequently, tenders were floated for the desilting work with specifications that allegedly matched Matprop’s equipment, limiting the options available to contractors.The tender reportedly stated that contractors would be paid based on the weight of silt and dredged material removed from the river. According to the police investigation, contractors who approached Matprop to purchase the equipment were instead directed towards Joshi and Kadam. The agency has alleged that the equipment was then rented out at inflated rates.The EOW had constituted a Special Investigation Team in August 2024 after allegations of irregularities were raised in connection with the desilting of the 17.84-km-long Mithi River. The investigation subsequently expanded to examine the alleged financial transactions, tendering process and the role of civic officials, contractors and intermediaries.Investigators have also alleged that records related to the quantity of silt removed from the river were manipulated, which could have resulted in contractors being paid higher amounts.Dino Morea’s questioning is part of the ongoing probe, and the investigation is continuing to establish the nature of his alleged links, if any, with the accused and the financial transactions under scrutiny. The actor has not been accused or convicted of wrongdoing in the case merely by virtue of being questioned by the investigating agency.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: In 1992, Donald Trump appeared in ‘Home Alone 2’: How his brief Plaza Hotel cameo became one of the film’s most remembered moments
articles.summary: When Home Alone 2: Lost in New York hit theatres in November 1992, audiences watched Macaulay Culkin’s Kevin McCallister navigate New York City after
articles.body: When Home Alone 2: Lost in New York hit theatres in November 1992, audiences watched Macaulay Culkin’s Kevin McCallister navigate New York City after accidentally ending up there alone. Among the film’s many memorable moments was a brief appearance by businessman Donald Trump at the Plaza Hotel, which he owned at the time.The cameo lasts only a few seconds. Kevin encounters Trump inside the hotel and asks him for directions to the lobby. Trump points him down the hallway and to the left before Kevin continues on his way. Despite its brevity, the scene has remained one of the most recognisable celebrity cameos in the Home Alone franchise.Why was Donald Trump in ‘Home Alone 2’?The circumstances surrounding the cameo have been disputed by Trump and the film’s director Chris Columbus. What is established is that the production filmed at the Plaza Hotel, which Trump owned at the time. The American Film Institute’s records also acknowledge the Plaza Hotel among the film’s special thanks.Columbus later said that getting permission to shoot inside the Plaza came with a condition that Trump appear in the film. In a 2020 interview, the director said Trump had effectively insisted that the hotel could only be used if he appeared in the movie. Columbus also recalled that the production initially considered removing the scene.However, when the filmmakers screened the movie for an audience, Columbus said viewers reacted enthusiastically when Trump appeared on screen. He therefore decided to keep the cameo.Trump has given a different account. In 2023, he denied that he had forced his way into the movie, saying that the filmmakers had repeatedly asked him to appear and that he initially did not want to do it. According to Trump’s account, he eventually agreed after the production team remained persistent.The seven-second sceneTrump’s role was extremely small. In the scene, Kevin is inside the Plaza Hotel and approaches Trump for help finding the lobby. Trump responds with directions, and the young protagonist walks away.The brief appearance has subsequently been described as roughly seven seconds long. It did not affect the film’s main storyline, but its connection to one of New York’s most famous hotels and Trump’s later prominence ensured that the moment remained widely discussed.‘Home Alone 2’ became a major box-office successThe sequel was released on November 20, 1992, with Chris Columbus directing and John Hughes writing and producing. It reunited Macaulay Culkin with Joe Pesci, Daniel Stern, Catherine O’Hara and other members of the original cast.The film became one of the biggest releases of 1992. It eventually earned more than $359 million worldwide and became a recurring Christmas favourite, helping turn the short Trump appearance into a scene that audiences continued to encounter during holiday re-runs.The cameo returned to the spotlight years laterTrump’s appearance gained renewed attention in 2019 when Canada’s CBC aired an edited version of Home Alone 2 without the scene. The broadcaster explained that the movie had been edited in 2014, along with other portions, to make room for commercials and that Trump’s cameo was removed because it was not essential to the plot.The explanation became particularly notable because Trump was president by 2019, and the removal prompted criticism from some of his supporters. Trump himself commented publicly on the missing scene at the time. The edit, however, had been made before he became president.Chris Columbus later said he wished the cameo was goneMore than three decades after the film’s release, Columbus revisited the cameo in a 2025 interview. The director said he regretted including it and described the appearance as something he wished had not been in the movie. He also reiterated his account that Trump had made appearing in the film a condition for the production to use the Plaza.Trump has continued to dispute Columbus’ version of events, maintaining that the filmmakers wanted him in the movie and that his appearance helped its success.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez custody war for their son: Actress’ alleged texts to ex-husband revealed; ‘I feel terrible about what happened’
articles.summary: Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez's ongoing custody dispute over their son Maceo intensifies with the revelation of alarming text messages. Discover the details of their custody war and the implications of the domestic violence allegations.
articles.body: The latest details in Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez's custody dispute come from a more personal source than a courtroom argument: their text messages. Messages between the former couple were included in the domestic violence restraining order filing Martinez made in Los Angeles Superior Court on Thursday, October 1, 2026. They show Berry and Martinez arguing about their 12-year-old son, Maceo, both before and after an alleged confrontation at Berry's home on Saturday, September 26.Martinez, 60, has accused Halle Berry, also 60, of physically abusing their son and is asking for sole custody. The allegations have not been proven in court, and Berry's attorney has strongly rejected his account.What Halle Berry allegedly texted Olivier MartinezAccording to the messages included in Olivier Martinez's court filing, the disagreement began after Maceo asked to be picked up early from Halle Berry's home.Martinez apparently contacted Berry about the change. Her response was not simply about the pickup. She questioned why her son wanted to leave and wrote, “No, I’m not ok with it. He wants to fight his mother?? What kind of kid are we raising?”She followed that with another message asking Martinez to question Maceo about his behaviour. “I’m his mother?” Berry allegedly wrote.The conversation then turned toward their relationship with their son. Olivier Martinez said he did not understand what was happening but questioned whether Halle Berry would keep Maceo at her home if he did not want to stay. Berry responded that she felt Maceo was treating her as though she had no authority.“He is disrespectful to me and feels I have no say on anything,” she allegedly wrote. “I’m just money bags! This is wrong and wrong!” It is an unusually revealing exchange because it captures the frustration between two parents in the middle of a much bigger dispute, rather than simply presenting the allegations made in court.Halle Berry says she felt terribleAnother message included in the filing was sent by Halle Berry on Sunday, September 27, 2026. She told Martinez that she had reached out to Maceo and wanted to speak with him. She also asked Martinez to encourage their son to talk to her.“I feel terrible about what happened last night as I know he does as well,” she allegedly wrote. The message came after Olivier Martinez's account of the September 26 incident.In his court filing, Martinez alleged that Berry had been arguing with Maceo while he was playing a virtual-reality game. He claimed the confrontation became physical and alleged that Berry put her hands around their son's neck and choked him.Olivier also claimed Maceo called him in a panic and asked him to pick him up. Text messages between Maceo and his father were included in the filing, with the boy allegedly writing, “Are u here please come.” These details are allegations contained in Martinez's filing, not established findings of the court.Halle Berry’s lawyer strongly denies Martinez’s claimsHalle Berry's response has been equally forceful. Her attorney, Marina Beck, described Olivier Martinez's filing as “entirely meritless and deliberately misleading” in a statement provided to PEOPLE. Beck also alleged that Martinez had previously violated court orders and interfered with therapeutic and educational interventions involving Maceo.Martinez's attorney, Patrick Baghdaserians, presented the opposite position. He said his client's “paramount concern is the health, welfare and the safety of the minor child” and described Martinez as a parent trying to protect his son.Neither side has agreed on what the September 26 incident means or how it should be understood.A custody dispute that has been going on for yearsThe latest filing did not come out of nowhere. Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez married on July 13, 2013, and welcomed Maceo later that year. They announced their split in 2015 and finalised their divorce in 2023.Their divorce agreement gave them joint legal custody. Berry was also ordered to pay Martinez $8,000 a month in child support, along with additional support tied to income above $2 million.The former couple had also previously turned to co-parenting therapy. Earlier court disputes centred on disagreements over parenting decisions and the way they communicated about Maceo.That history makes the new text messages more revealing. They are not simply about one pickup or one argument. They show two parents who were already struggling to agree about their son's behaviour, boundaries and where he should be.What happens next for Halle Berry and Olivier Martinez?A Los Angeles County judge granted Olivier Martinez a temporary restraining order on October 1, 2026. The order did not completely prevent Halle Berry from contacting Maceo, but it temporarily restricted her visitation while the case moves forward. A further hearing is scheduled for October 16, 2026. The court has also ordered the former couple to participate in mediation.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.summary: Saina Chatterjee’s Pujo memories come with the sound of dhaak, her father dancing beside her and her mother capturing the moment on camera.
articles.body: Saina Chatterjee’s Pujo memories come with the sound of dhaak, her father dancing beside her and her mother capturing the moment on camera. articles.title: R Madhavan, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal hail pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for saving 174 people on a flydubai flight
articles.summary: Several film personalities, including R Madhavan, Shilpa Shetty, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal, have applauded Indian pilot Captain Smit
articles.body: Several film personalities, including R Madhavan, Shilpa Shetty, Vijay Deverakonda, Ravi Kishan and Paresh Rawal, have applauded Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his bravery. He allegedly stopped his co-pilot from crashing a Flydubai flight that carried 174 passengers, 27 of them children.R Madhavan and Vijay Deverakonda lead the tributesR Madhavan shared Prime Minister Narendra Modi's statement on the incident and wished the captain a speedy recovery. He called him "a true hero."Vijay praised the pilot's calm in a life-threatening situation. "May God protect you and bless you, Captain. What you faced and what you did is incredible. Along with everyone else on that flight," he wrote.Ravi Kishan, Paresh Rawal and others reactActor-politician Ravi Kishan spoke of the captain's dedication and strength. "Captain Smit Machchhar is the epitome of unwavering loyalty to duty, indomitable courage, and extraordinary wisdom (sic)," he wrote, adding that the pilot's actions are a matter of great national pride.Paresh Rawal played on the pilot's surname, recalling a well-known dialogue by Nana Patekar from the 1994 film 'Krantiveer'. "Remembering NANA PATEKAR'S FAMOUS DIALOGUE: Ek Machhhar Aadmiko...!" he posted.Shilpa Shetty also extended her support to those affected. "Heart goes out to everyone affected. And immense respect for Captain Smit Machchhar for bringing over 170 lives to safety," she wrote.Jackie Shroff paid tribute to the captain and everyone who helped avoid the disaster. “Some heroes work in silence! All my respects to Captain Smit Machchhar and the other brave heroes for saving lives and averting a massive tragedy," he said.PM Narendra Modi's messageAlong with Narendra Modi, actors Sonam Kapoor and Kangana Ranaut also took to social media to appreciate the pilot. The Prime Minister tweeted, “Captain Smit Machchhar has shown the world the highest form of courage. Without fearing for his own life, he fought valiantly and prevented another 9/11-like attack from happening. 140 crore Indians salute Captain Smit and are praying for his well-being."What happened on the flightThe flydubai flight was headed from Dubai to Tel Aviv but was diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. According to Israeli officials, the co-pilot attacked Captain Machchhar in the cockpit and stabbed him.Though badly injured and bleeding on the cockpit floor, the Mumbai-born pilot reportedly managed to trigger the emergency release and open the cockpit door. This let cabin crew and passengers rush in and overpower the attacker. Two off-duty flydubai pilots travelling as passengers then landed the aircraft safely.Captain Machchhar is now being treated at a hospital in Tabuk, where doctors continue to monitor his condition.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Paramount’s Warner Bros. megamerger will just be called Skydance
articles.summary: David Ellison doesn’t want a ‘new corporate identity’ to overshadow Warner Bros. and Paramount’s brands.
articles.body: Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison has announced that the company will just be called Skydance when it completes its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery next week. In a post on X, Ellison writes that “we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.” Earlier this week, a judge approved the settlement Paramount reached with California and 11 other states that sued over the planned acquisition, clearing the last major hurdle blocking the deal. Under the deal, Paramount must release a minimum number of theatrical films over the next five years, starting with 30 annually in years one and two. Ahead of the close, Paramount has also appointed Ynon Kreiz, the former chairman and CEO of Mattel, as the co-CEO of the soon-to-be even bigger company. The deal is expected to close on October 6th. Here’s Ellison’s full announcement: > What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. > Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history — we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling. > We chose this name for a few important reasons. First and foremost, as we bring Paramount and Warner Bros. together, we wanted to preserve what has made each of these studios iconic. Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations. We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight. > We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks. At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance. > I couldn’t be more excited about what we’re going to build together.

articles.title: Gordon Ramsay admits real reason he was crying while walking daughter down the aisle
articles.summary: Gordon Ramsay reveals feeling "second best" after walking Holly Ramsay down the aisle and jokes about what really made him cry at the wedding.
articles.body: Gordon Ramsay opened up about the bittersweet experience of giving away his daughter, Holly Ramsay, at her wedding. Holly, 26, married Olympic swimmer Adam Peaty, 31, in December 2025 after the couple announced their engagement in 2024. The 59-year-old celebrity chef shares Holly, her twin brother Jack, daughters Megan, 28, and Matilda, 24, and sons Oscar, 7, and Jesse, 2, with his wife, Tana Ramsay, 52, whom he married in 1996. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, Ramsay, who is starring in season two of Apple TV's "Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars," reflected on the close bonds that he shares with his three daughters and explained why he was left feeling "second best" after he walked Holly down the aisle. GORDON RAMSAY SAYS ‘THE MOST IMPORTANT THING’ HE TAUGHT HIS SIX KIDS HAD NOTHING TO DO WITH COOKING "You grow up with these gorgeous girls and you teach them. I said to them, from an early age, they must have been 7 or 8 years of age, ‘The earlier you tell me, the more I can f---ing do," he recalled. "They ignore you for two or three years," Ramsay continued. "But when they get to 11 or 12, ‘Hey daddy, you know what he said to me? The earlier you told me, the more you can do, I have a problem. Can I talk to you about it?’" KELLY RIPA, MARK CONSUELOS SHARE BLUNT ADVICE FOR COUPLES PLANNING A BIG WEDDING "Bang, then we're in,'" he added with a smile. "Then you're like that, you're sort of the BFF, right? Then you're a cool f---ing dad, then you're perfect. But when you walk them down the aisle, and you're minutes away from not being the number one guy in their life, and you're handing them over, man, that hits. That absolutely hits." "So you have to understand that that relationship with your daughter is borrowed time before there's another man in their lives. Another partner in their life, that you become second best." WATCH: GORDON RAMSAY ADMITS REAL REASON HE WAS CRYING WHILE WALKING DAUGHTER DOWN THE AISLE The "Hell's Kitchen" star noted that as a father of six, he will have to experience those moments multiple times in the future. "I have ages to go through all that s---," he said. "Three boys and three girls." Ramsay, who is famous for his fiery temper and tough demeanor in the kitchen, admitted to becoming emotional at Holly's wedding but joked that it was not for the reason that most people would expect. "I was like a sack of f---ing custard walking down that bloody — that line — into that church. 60 meters!" he recalled. "And I was looking at all these flowers overlooking the pews and thinking, ‘S---, this is expensive!' Everyone thought I was crying because I was giving her away. I was more crying with the f---ing cost of the flower bill, and where are they going tomorrow? We're paying all this money for 90 minutes, these flowers." DANA PERINO: FIVE IMPORTANT LESSONS FROM MY FATHER FOR EVERY PROUD GIRL DAD Ramsay quipped that his tears dried up once he realized that the flowers could be repurposed for a good cause. "We got the flowers donated to the local hospital and that stopped me crying," he said. "And then I handed her over, and I celebrated like no tomorrow, because that daughter was expensive." CLINT BLACK AND LISA HARTMAN BLACK'S ONE RULE THAT HAS KEPT THEIR MARRIAGE STRONG FOR NEARLY 35 YEARS Holly and Peaty's wedding took place on Dec. 27, 2025, at The Abbey Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul in Bath, England. During a January interview with People, Ramsay admitted that he was nervous about giving his father-of-the-bride speech. "It's tough, honestly — I mean, being a dad with three daughters, you dream of that moment. That moment arrives, and you're just like a hot mess," he told the outlet. "The speech was perfect. It went well. You got to find that sort of — you've got to be warm, emotional ... It was just a tough gig." Tilly told People that Ramsay spent about an hour rehearsing his speech in front of her on Christmas Eve. She said that while Ramsay pored over every word, ultimately "no tweaks were needed." "It was perfect," Tilly said. "It made everybody cry." ‘CHARLIE’S ANGELS’ STAR JACLYN SMITH LIVED APART FROM HER HUSBAND FOR 17 YEARS DURING THEIR 35-YEAR LOVE STORY Holly wore three different dresses on her wedding day, including her mother's gown from her 1996 nuptials with Ramsay. The TV personality told People that seeing Holly in Tana's wedding dress came as "a bit of a shock." While speaking with British Vogue in January, Holly noted that wearing the gown during her father-daughter dance with Ramsay was especially meaningful because "the last time Dad saw this dress was when he danced with my mom at their wedding." At the time, Holly told the outlet that Ramsay became emotional whenever she discussed the wedding leading up to her big day. "Dad cries every time I talk about the wedding," she said. "The other day I was asking him which car he and I would take to the church, and he welled up immediately." Though Holly is the first of Ramsay's six children to walk down the aisle, he will soon have to give another daughter away. In an August appearance on "Live with Kelly and Mark," he revealed that Megan was engaged. During his interview with Fox News Digital, Ramsay noted that he needed to start preparing for Megan's nuptials. "I've got to get my dance act together, especially with another wedding coming up next year," he said. "Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars," which is executive produced by Ramsay, made its debut on Apple TV in October 2025. Hosted by food expert Jesse Burgess, the documentary series follows chefs around the world as they pursue Michelin stars while balancing the personal and professional sacrifices required to achieve culinary excellence. While speaking with Fox News Digital, Ramsay admitted that his own pursuit of perfection in the kitchen had come at a cost. Looking back, the "MasterChef" star reflected on the biggest sacrifice that he made while building his restaurant empire. "Time," he said. "You become one of the most, sort of, you know, selfish individuals because you need to focus. And so I'd say the sacrifice was less time with the family straight off the bat." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "There's a lot of situations in ‘Knife Edge,' you'll see families working together. That's actually harder," he continued. "My wife and I decided that 'Look, the time we have is little, but it'd be quality.' It won't be great, long time, but it would be quality. And then my kids appreciate the time they had with me." "They didn't see me seven nights a week," Ramsay said. "I didn't do the school runs. I wasn't doing the dinners and the goodbyes and the plays and all the nativities. I couldn't do that. And so, don't forget when all your mates are out celebrating, you're working because they're either eating at the restaurants or out going to another restaurant." "So yeah, I'd say time, the biggest, the most expensive ingredient in the world, time," he added. "And you have to sacrifice that time." Ramsay, whose restaurants currently hold nine Michelin stars worldwide, has earned a total of 17 Michelin stars over the course of his career. His flagship Restaurant Gordon Ramsay in London has held the maximum three Michelin stars continuously since 2001. Ramsay's portfolio gained a ninth star earlier this year when Restaurant Gordon Ramsay High in London's Bishopsgate area earned its first Michelin star in the 2026 Michelin Guide. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE According to the official synopsis, season two of "Knife Edge" "follows 16 restaurants at pivotal moments in their journeys: A chef and his family risk everything to put a tiny island on Michelin’s map. Two generations of a legendary culinary family pursue recognition on their own terms. Two chefs voluntarily give up their Star when they open a new restaurant and have just 52 days to win it back." "One sandwich shop transforms into a fine-dining restaurant each night, while a young couple seeks to put Filipino cuisine at the center of one of America’s most competitive dining scenes. Their circumstances could hardly be more different, yet each faces the same uncertainty: when Michelin makes its decision, will everything they have strived for be enough?" Ramsay noted that "Knife Edge" pulls back the curtain on the countless hours of preparation and discipline that diners rarely see before a meal reaches the table. "Finally, now we have a show on Apple that really unfolds that unscripted drama and follows the highs and lows, the emotions, the pressures that these restaurants are under — especially today," he said. The celebrity chef told Fox News Digital that he hopes the show gives viewers a new appreciation for the commitment behind every Michelin-starred meal. "I'd love the audience to take away from ‘Knife Edge' season 2 the understanding of pursuit for perfection and the price they pay is extraordinary," Ramsay said. "And then to understand properly, the commitment to perfection. You go to games and live sports, and you see that energy and the excitement and the touchdowns and the medals and the ceremony. It's the exact same for a restaurant. That you don't even see." articles.title: Sanjeev Kumar did C-grade films as he was broke, lent Rs 96 lakhs to his friends, 5-6 lakhs to Shatrughan Sinha: 'He suffered two heart attacks when he met Sulakshana Pandit'
articles.summary: Sanjeev Kumar remains one of Hindi cinema’s most respected actors, remembered for his performances in films such as ‘Sholay’, ‘Aandhi’, ‘Trishul’,
articles.body: Sanjeev Kumar remains one of Hindi cinema’s most respected actors, remembered for his performances in films such as ‘Sholay’, ‘Aandhi’, ‘Trishul’, ‘Koshish’ and ‘Mausam’. However, before achieving stardom, the actor went through a difficult financial phase and reportedly took up whatever work came his way. Journalist Hanif Zaveri recently recalled that Sanjeev was so financially strained during the early years of his career that he even worked in C-grade films to support his family.In a conversation on the Meri Saheli Podcast’s YouTube channel, Zaveri spoke about Sanjeev’s struggling years, when he was trying to establish himself in the film industry while his family was also dealing with financial difficulties. According to him, the actor owned just two sets of clothes at the time, while his mother was trying to cope with his father’s failing business."He didn't know that the films he was doing were C-grade. He was quite broke, so he was doing whatever work he could get," recalled Hanif Zaveri.Despite experiencing financial hardships himself, Sanjeev was known for being generous towards those around him. Zaveri claimed that the actor lent Rs 96 lakh to several friends over the years, but never received the money back. He also recalled instances of Sanjeev paying for his driver’s wedding and gifting a car to a friend."He gave Rs 96 lakh away as loans to his friends, who never paid him back. He paid for his driver's wedding. He gifted a car to one of his friends. When Sanjeev made his will, he kept Rs 2 lakh aside for his driver's son's education. People who are miserly don't do this. He was simply against unnecessary expenditure," added Zaveri.Zaveri further recalled how Sanjeev helped fellow actors and filmmakers without expecting anything in return. He said the actor gave money to Shatrughan Sinha when he needed it, even though Sinha had not asked him for financial help. He also claimed that Sanjeev gave money to filmmaker Boney Kapoor without any formal paperwork."When Shatrughan Sinha needed money, Sanjeev Kumar gave it to him even though Shatrughan hadn't asked for it. Boney Kapoor needed money too, so he gave it to him as well, without any documentation or formalities. After Sanjeev died, Boney returned the money to his family. Even the family didn't know he had given that money," he said.The journalist also spoke about the friendship between Sanjeev Kumar and Shatrughan Sinha. He recalled how Sanjeev supported Sinha during the early stages of his career after the latter returned from the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII)."They shared a deep friendship. When Sanjeev got to know that Shatrughan needed money, he was the first person to help out. He gave around Rs 5-7 lakh," added the journalist.While Sanjeev eventually went on to work with some of the biggest filmmakers in the industry and establish himself as a celebrated actor, his personal life remained complicated. Zaveri spoke about his relationships with Hema Malini and Nutan before discussing his later relationship with actor-singer Sulakshana Pandit.According to Zaveri, Sanjeev chose not to marry Sulakshana because he was convinced that he would have a short life. He had already suffered two heart attacks by the time they met and reportedly believed that he would not live beyond the age of 50 because several men in his family had died young."He had already suffered two heart attacks by the time he met Sulakshana Pandit. He did not want to marry anyone. He believed that he had a short life, and he felt this way because all the men in his family had died before the age of 50. He believed that he too would die before turning 50, so he did not want to get married and spoil someone else's life. That was the only reason why he did not marry her," said Hanif.Sanjeev Kumar passed away on November 6, 1985, at the age of 47.
